newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium ends higher, lead sinks below $800.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium ends higher, lead sinks below $800.

text.p: Most LME base metals gyrated in sleepy price bands during Tuesday afternoon, but lead dived below the psychological $800 level and aluminium bucked its earlier trend to close slightly stronger.
Aluminium probed the lower end of its range in the morning but edged higher during the afternoon.
After a brief flurry of buying on the afternoon kerb, three month prices ended at their high of $1,482, a gain of $4.
"That's a relatively good close and with the technical indicators swinging higher I don't think there's much selling left," said William Adams, analyst at broker Rudolf Wolff.
Prices would have to break above $1,500, however, before the picture began looking constructive for the upside, analysts say.
On the downside, further weakness may target a test of $1,450/60, the lows of mid-July, after the 10-day moving average bearishly crossed below the 30-day average last week, chartists said.
Three month copper was held captive in a tiny $5 range between $1,940 and $1,945 per tonne, ending the afternoon kerb at $1,944, a loss of $5 from Friday.
Spreads were a fraction softer, finishing the day at around a $37 backwardation compared to $42 on Friday.
Adams said spreads could widen as the market moved towards tight dates in early September, when players who shorted the market in the wake of the Sumitomo sell-off may have to roll over positions.
The market would also be watching the results of a strike vote by workers in Codelco's Salvador division, which was expected at 0230 GMT on Wednesday.
But near-term prices were seen holding in the $1,900-$1,970 range which has trapped prices for nearly a month, dealers said.
Lead broke below the $800 level after after edging down all day, closing at $795, a loss of $12 from Friday.
"It might carry on drifting down towards $780," said Adams.
Most of the market is bullish on lead in the medium to long term and the market got a little over-extended, he added.
Bargain hunting could soon prop up prices, traders said.
Nickel eased back after its recent strong gains, with three month values closing at the low of $7,340, down $90.
Analysts say the market may need to consolidate since an expected increase in physical demand may take time to gather steam.
Zinc initially crept lower, hitting bottom at support of $1,020, but ended at its high of $1,025, up $1.
A close below $1,020 would signal a fall towards the March downtrend, which currently appears at $995, according to Harry Creates, chartist for broker AMT.
Resistance is seen at $1,030, the late July downtrend, he added.
Tin hardly moved, finishing at $6,175 up $5, with key resistance pegged at $6,200.
Alloy was indicated at $1,275/80 versus $1,285 on Friday.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8065
